summary: Discovery call to scope Dedicated GPU capacity for Midland Capital's in-house LLM features. Primary concerns: tenant isolation, burst capacity and autoscale, latency SLOs vs cost, security/KMS and audit logs. Redwood AE+SE walked through capacity tiers, burst options, routing/fallback, caching, and proposed benchmark pilot. Agreed next steps include sending pricing and security docs and scheduling a benchmark run.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Rajat Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Midland Head of ML), Marcus Doyle (Infra Lead), Priya Rao (Security), Alan Wu (Data Eng)

[00:00] Sophie: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Sophie from Redwood, i'll run through scope, rajat's our se and he'll handle the technical bits. how's everyone's morning?
[00:18] Laura: Morning, we're excited to talk. we've been evaluating hosted vs dedi, mainly leaning dedi for isolation.
[00:30] Marcus: yeah we have regulatory constraints; data cannot leave our VPC for some models.
[00:38] Sophie: understood. quick agenda - 1) current infra & traffic profile, 2) dedicated capacity options, 3) burst and autoscale patterns, 4) security/compliance, 5) next steps. sound good?
[00:50] Laura: yep
[01:05] Rajat: quick question, Laura — what are your peak QPS and typical sequence lengths? that drives kernel selection and batch sizing.
[01:20] Laura: in prod we see about 400 qps baseline for inference endpoints, peaks to ~1.6k during end of day reconciles; sequences average 80 tokens, some longer 300+ for doc summarization.
[01:40] Marcus: and latency budget is 300ms 95th for customer-facing features, internal batched jobs can be longer.
[01:50] Rajat: okay that's super helpful. baseline 400 qps and 1.6k bursts — sounds like a dedicated pool with burst capacity makes sense.
[02:10] Sophie: we have Dedicated tiers — reserved GPU pools you own with optional burst capacity into a shared pool. you can pin models and set rollout policies.
[02:28] Marcus: what's the difference between burst and autoscale?
[02:34] Rajat: autoscale is horizontal for the dedicated pool based on queued work / utilization; burst lets you overflow to our multi-tenant capacity for short windows. there is a policy to cap cost/latency tradeoffs.
[02:56] Laura: how short is "short"? our bursts sometimes last 20-30 minutes.
[03:02] Rajat: we typically support bursts up to a few hours depending on contract and commit. for 20-30m it's well within expected usage; we'd propose a committed baseline with a burst buffer sized for your 1.6k peak.
[03:20] Priya: from security: we need to know encryption at rest and KMS options, audit log retention, and whether keys live in our HSM.
[03:33] Sophie: yes — Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations in Private deployments; for Dedicated we offer KMS integration options and audit logs with configurable retention. we'll share the SOC2/ISO packet after this call.
[03:50] Marcus: data residency — some models must not leave the EU. can routing pin region?
[03:58] Rajat: yes, smart routing can keep requests regionally pinned; you can set policies to route to EU-only nodes. fallback models can be limited to compliant variants.
[04:15] Alan: curious about quantization/throughput — do you support int8 or 4-bit pipelines? we need cost savings.
[04:23] Rajat: yes, runtime supports quantization-friendly execution paths. we'll recommend profiles per workload. for heavy summarization 4-bit often works; we do kernel selection and pipeline tuning.
[04:35] Laura: what about KV cache, we've seen caching help for chat flows.
[04:40] Rajat: we have prefix/KV caching and can pin cache to the dedicated pool to reduce token cost and tune latency. watch out for cache warming during rollouts.
[04:55] Sophie: can i confirm stakeholders? Laura (ML), Marcus (Infra), Priya (Security), Alan (Data).
[05:05] Marcus: yep
[05:18] Sophie: ok i'll share pricing tiers — typically for your profile we'd propose a 2x reserved baseline that covers 95% of traffic and a burst pool for the remaining peaks.
[05:30] Laura: 2x seems conservative, why 2x?
[05:34] Rajat: because of request variance and seq length distribution; for lower latency SLOs you need headroom for KV cache misses and model warmup. we can model it with your traffic traces in the benchmark.
[05:55] Marcus: can we run a pilot / bench with representative traffic?
[06:00] Sophie: absolutely, typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: we set up a dedicated pool, run benchmark and production-mirroring, and gauge cost/latency.
[06:12] Laura: ok logistics — we prefer a day-of-week for the benchmark when end-of-day peaks happen, maybe next Wed.
[06:22] Sophie: noted (2026-03-11 suggested).
[06:30] Priya: how are identities/SSO handled? we need SCIM and SAML for RBAC.
[06:36] Sophie: Redwood Console supports SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM for user provisioning and role-based access. Dedicated has per-tenant RBAC and audit trails.
[06:50] Marcus: licensing and contract — are there min terms?
[06:55] Sophie: for Dedicated we do monthly or annual reserved commits; pilot can be month-to-month, production commit gives better pricing. i'll include contract samples with pricing.
[07:10] Alan: on integration — how do we route traffic from our infra? via VPC peering or private link?
[07:18] Rajat: we support VPC peering, private link, or a Private deployment where control plane is customer-managed. for dedicated you can choose VPC peering and private endpoints.
[07:32] Laura: if we go Private/on-prem later, how portable are model artifacts and configs?
[07:38] Rajat: we keep model versions and rollout configs abstracted; artifacts can be exported and we have an on-prem package for regulated workloads. some kernel optimizations are hardware-specific but configs are portable.
[07:54] Marcus: regarding observability — can we get token-level cost breakout and per-model latency dashboards?
[08:00] Sophie: yes Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards and tracing hooks; we can provide sample dashboards and export metrics to your prometheus/grafana.
[08:12] Laura: what about fallback policies — if capacity constrained can we auto-fallback to cheaper models?
[08:17] Rajat: yes, smart routing supports fallback variants and can degrade gracefully. you control the fallback order by policy.
[08:30] Priya: compliance question: do you support SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001?
[08:36] Sophie: yes we hold SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001; will share certificate and security pack.
[08:45] Marcus: cost question — what's typical $/token for dedicated vs hosted?
[08:50] Sophie: it varies by commit size and model. generally dedicated reserved pools reduce unit cost by 20–40% depending on utilization and quantization. we'll send a pricing matrix.
[09:05] Alan: for the bench we'll want to test 400 qps baseline and synthetic peaks to 1.6k, with sequences 80–300 tokens.
[09:14] Rajat: perfect, we'll ask you to provide a small sample trace and an anonymized traffic histogram.
[09:22] Laura: timeline — decision in 4 weeks, prefer to run pilot before commit.
[09:28] Sophie: good, we can align.
[09:35] [speaker overlap] Marcus: quick — what about SLA on latency?
[09:40] Rajat: we offer latency targets as part of Dedicated SLA; specifics depend on model family and commit.
[09:48] Laura: any known caveats? rollouts causing cache misses we already heard about — anything else?
[09:54] Rajat: warmup mainly, and cross-tenant noise if you use burst into shared pool — we enforce policies to minimize noise but dedicated baseline avoids it.
[10:10] Sophie: ok moving to procurement/legal — priya, any procurement constraints we should know?
[10:18] Priya: vendor questionnaires will come, need DPA, security annex, and our internal legal needs at +2 weeks after pilot.
[10:28] Sophie: we'll provide DPA and security annex with the packet.
[10:34] Laura: anything else on the infra side? Marcus: autoscale thresholds — how instant is scale up/down?
[10:40] Rajat: scale up is typically within a few minutes for horizontal scaling; model startup and kv warming add latency hair. autoscale is configurable on utilization and queue length.
[10:54] Marcus: how do we monitor GPU utilization and set alerts?
[11:00] Sophie: Console exposes GPU/utilization metrics and you can export alerts to slack/pagerduty.
[11:12] Alan: if we compress models to 4-bit do we get ~2-3x throughput?
[11:18] Rajat: it's workload dependent — often 1.5x-3x improvement; we'll quantify in the bench.
[11:28] Laura: ok let's summarize and next steps.
[11:33] Sophie: recap: Redwood to send pricing, SOC2/ISO/KMS notes, bench plan; Midland to send traffic traces and QPS/latency targets; schedule bench for 2026-03-11.
[11:48] Laura: sounds good.
[11:52] Sophie: any outstanding blockers?
[11:55] Priya: none besides vendor questionnaire timeline.
[12:00] Sophie: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email with artifacts.

End transcript. Notes: transcription has a few mis-hearings ("KV cash" sometimes in auto transcript), speaker labels occasionally generic in exported file.
